title: Define semantic review providers and risk routing

requirement.summary: Implement the Revision 4 architecture as strict vendor-neutral Provider capability, semantic risk route, and advisory review result contracts with zero-call low risk, active-Agent medium-risk self-review, optional independent high-risk review, and explicit human/lower-assurance/setup choices when independence is unavailable.

objective.rationale: The natural-language Adapter needs a trustworthy, cross-agent contract for who supplies semantic inference and what assurance is available before any real model or vendor integration is selected.

goal: Add an accepted Provider/risk-routing ADR, three strict model-free contracts and Python reference logic, cross-agent capability fixtures, fail-closed route/result binding, and protecting tests without calling a model or configuring credentials.
non_goals: Do not call, bundle, download, benchmark, select, or recommend a real LLM, model SDK, endpoint, gateway, account, or vendor.
Do not create or read API keys, environment secrets, global user configuration, repository Provider configuration, billing data, or external network state.
Do not implement a production materializer, sub-agent runtime, background process, host callback, UI, or hosted AgentGov Reviewer.
Do not treat same-agent review as independent, silently downgrade high-risk assurance, or allow Provider identity to imply correctness.

Do not allow an LLM result to become deterministic proof, select a human option, mutate project state, or authorize code, scope, exceptions, Git, publication, release, deployment, production, or external writes.
Do not change stable 0.2.1, immutable v0.3.0rc1, release metadata, workflows, consumer repositories, or external systems.
acceptance_signals: An accepted ADR owns the model-free Core, host Provider, risk-tier, assurance disclosure, missing-independence, privacy/cost ownership, advisory-only result, and denied-authority decisions without selecting a vendor.

A strict semantic-review-provider-capabilities contract declares portable Provider/source identity, availability, supported self or independent mode, exact independence level, cost owner, retention/external-transfer boundaries, forbidden raw content, and fully denied authority.
Codex, Claude Code, generic IDE independent-review, and unavailable-Provider fixtures all validate through the same contract while Core source and schemas contain no vendor enum or special case.

A strict semantic-review-route deterministically maps low risk to no semantic call, medium risk to available active-Agent self-review, and high risk to an available independent Reviewer with at least isolated context.

High risk with no qualifying independent Reviewer returns exactly human review, explicit lower-assurance self-review, and Provider setup choices; none is selected and the route cannot be described as independently reviewed.

A strict semantic-review-result is accepted only for the exact routed Provider and route digest, reports only evidence-linked ADVISORY observations and disclosed assurance, excludes raw/sensitive/host-local content, and grants no project or external authority.

Unknown fields, invalid mode/independence combinations, unavailable execution, same-agent independent claims, stale route/provider bindings, non-advisory semantics, silent downgrade, and authority drift fail before any result is accepted.
No code path performs network I/O, loads credentials, starts an agent, calls a model, writes repository/runtime state, or applies a human choice.
Affected source-of-truth and public documentation accurately distinguishes implemented contracts from still-open production Provider integration.
Focused/full tests, schemas, current-task, scope, repository, compile, and diff validation pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_semantic_review tests.test_host_interaction tests.test_human_decision tests.test_agent_skills tests.test_task_contract tests.test_user_documentation tests.test_portfolio_docs -v

items: Contract fields could accidentally present model provenance or independence as evidence of correctness.
Routing could silently treat a current-Agent pass as independent review or continue high-risk work without disclosed assurance loss.
Provider metadata could leak credentials, raw conversation, host paths, model secrets, or undeclared source content.
Adding contracts before real host evidence could create protocol weight unless limited to the next executable vertical slice.

stop_conditions: Stop if low or medium risk requires a newly configured second model or external account.
Stop if independent review can use same-turn context or an unavailable/self-review-only Provider.
Stop if an absent Reviewer can silently route to lower assurance without a human-owned choice.
Stop if raw conversation, source content, credentials, secrets, model prompts, or absolute host paths enter Core contracts.
Stop if any Provider/result field grants project, task, architecture, session, code, scope, exception, Git, publication, release, deployment, production, or external-write authority.
Stop before any model call, Provider setup, network access, external write, Git write, publication, release, deployment, or consumer mutation.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed the completed contract slice and explicitly approved moving to the next active-Agent self-review materializer requirement on 2026-08-06.
